standard_prerequisites.name: The composite of the functor Can with H^0 is isomorphic to the identity functor on the category of modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Disposes of one of the two composites, so that only the composite starting from a glued object has to be analysed.

standard_prerequisites.name: After inverting one of the generators the comparison morphism becomes an isomorphism, and its kernel and cokernel are then systems concentrated in the first component
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the analysis of the kernel and cokernel of the comparison morphism to systems of the special form with only the S-component present.

standard_prerequisites.name: A system of the form with only the first component present has the property that H^0 of it is that component, and H^0 is left exact, so the exactness computation gives that the kernel vanishes
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the comparison morphism is injective, which is the first half of the proof that it is an isomorphism.

standard_prerequisites.name: For an I-power torsion module the canonical map from the tensor product with S is an isomorphism, and extensions of the module by the image of H^0 can be realized inside the glued category
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the commutative diagram with exact rows whose middle term gives a module E with Can(E) isomorphic to the glued object.

core_obligations: Record that one of the two composites is already known to be isomorphic to the identity functor, and take an arbitrary object of the glued category with its components, the module M', the modules M_i over the localizations and the transition maps alpha_i and alpha_ij (proof lines 24823-24828).

Construct the natural comparison morphism Psi from the object built out of H^0 of the glued object to the glued object itself, using the compatible maps that define H^0, and announce that the goal is to prove it is an isomorphism (proof lines 24829-24839).

Localize at one of the generators and use the two earlier lemmas to see that Psi becomes an isomorphism after inverting f_i; conclude that the kernel and the cokernel of Psi are systems with only the first component present, that the kernel vanishes because H^0 of such a system is that component and H^0 is left exact, so that Psi is injective (proof lines 24841-24849).

Convert the vanishing of the kernel into a short exact sequence and deduce a description of the modules M_i as localizations of H^0, then use that the cokernel is I-power torsion and invariant under tensoring with S, together with the extension lemma, to obtain the displayed commutative diagram with exact rows (proof lines 24851-24874).

Read off from the diagram that the middle term E gives an object whose image under Can is isomorphic to the glued object, which completes the proof that the two functors are quasi-inverse equivalences (proof lines 24874-24878).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the composite starting from a glued object and build the comparison morphism Psi from H^0 of that object (proof lines 24823-24839).
Localize at a generator to see that the kernel and cokernel of Psi are concentrated in the first component, and conclude injectivity from left exactness of H^0 (proof lines 24841-24849).

Turn the exact sequence into a description of the local components, use that the cokernel is power torsion and apply the extension lemma to produce the diagram with exact rows (proof lines 24851-24874).
Conclude that the middle term of that diagram maps under Can to the given glued object, so the comparison morphism is an isomorphism (proof lines 24875-24878).
difficulty_reason: The statement is the main equivalence theorem for the glued category attached to a flat ring map R -> S and a finitely generated ideal I with R over I isomorphic to S over IS: the functor Can and the functor H^0 are quasi-inverse equivalences between modules over R and the glued category (statement lines 24812-24821). The proof has to exhibit the second composite as the identity, which it does by localizing the comparison morphism at each generator so that the kernel and cokernel become systems concentrated in the first component, deducing injectivity from left exactness of H^0, then turning the resulting exact sequence into a description of the local components and finally constructing a module E from an extension of the power torsion cokernel by the image of H^0 whose image under Can is the given object (proof lines 24823-24878). The two genuinely independent inputs, namely the identification of the comparison after localization and the extension lemma for power torsion modules along the flat cover, are what make the argument nontrivial, and the whole construction of E is inside the counted span. The proof refers four times to earlier lemmas of the same chapter, carried as navigation stubs.
